title: dedicated-autoscaler: add priority routing controls, burst smoothing, and utilization reporting enhancements
author: Alex Kim
description:
Motivation: customers running Dedicated capacity want stronger guarantees for tail latency and predictable throughput when high-priority workloads spike. This PR adds three coordinated changes: 1) priority routing controls for the dedicated autoscaler so fleets can reserve burst capacity for higher-priority tenants; 2) token-bucket smoothing (burst smoothing) to reduce noisy autoscaler oscillation on transient spikes; and 3) enhanced utilization reporting (per-priority and per-fleet) so SREs and customers can reason about throttling, burst consumption, and wasted capacity.

What this changes (high level):
- Autoscaler: new priority-aware token buckets and routing policy. Added config fields dedicated_autoscaler.priority_buckets and dedicated_autoscaler.priority_routing.enable_fallback. Default behavior preserves current fairness for clusters without config.
- Token-bucket smoothing: implement exponential smoothing on observed request rates with a configurable smoothing_alpha and a minimum sustained window to avoid reacting to single-request bursts.
- Reporting: surface new metrics (dedicated_autoscaler.priority_capacity{priority}, dedicated_autoscaler.burst_consumed{priority}, dedicated_autoscaler.smoothing_factor) and emit structured events to the observability pipeline for per-tenant reporting. Update console dashboards to include priority breakdown and burst consumption graphs.
- API/Config: add an RFC-style schema for priority buckets (priority label, guaranteed_tokens, burst_tokens, refill_rate) and backward-compatible validation/upgrade logic.
- Tests: unit tests for bucket math and smoothing, integration tests for routing/fallback and end-to-end e2e that simulates mixed-priority load.

Compatibility and migration notes:
- New config fields are optional. Clusters without the priority config will continue to use the previous autoscaler behavior.
- For clusters that enable priority routing, there is a recommended migration plan in docs/ops/dedicated-autoscaler-migration.md (included in this PR) which outlines a canary rollout and a smoke test checklist.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement priority token buckets and routing policy in autoscaler service
- [x] Add smoothing algorithm and expose tuning knobs
- [x] Wire metrics through observability pipeline and add dashboard JSON
- [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests
- [x] Docs and migration guide
- [x] Backwards-compatible validation

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: misconfigured priority buckets could starve normal workloads. Mitigation: validation warns when guaranteed_tokens exceed fleet capacity and console will display warnings; default buckets are conservative.
- Risk: smoothing may increase time to react to sustained load. Mitigation: minimum sustained window and explicit alpha knobs allow tuning per-fleet.

References: Linear ENG-1423, related PRs on utilization/reporting (see pr-472500, pr-523450), ops runbook updates.

services/autoscaler/src/smoothing.rs: +pub fn smooth_rate(prev: f64, sample: f64, alpha: f64) -> f64 { prev * (1.0 - alpha) + sample * alpha }

conversation: Priya Natarajan (reviewer): Can we add a safety valve in the console that disables priority routing per-fleet? I want an operator toggle to quickly revert.
Alex Kim (author): Added per-fleet toggle in charts/dedicated-autoscaler/values.yaml and console route honors it. Also added a runtime flag --disable-priority-routing for emergency rollbacks.
Jordan Lee (reviewer): The smoothing alpha default is 0.3; can we document a recommended range for GPU-heavy workloads where burstiness is higher?
Alex Kim (author): Added guidance to docs/ops/dedicated-autoscaler-migration.md recommending 0.2-0.5 for typical CPU-bound workloads and 0.1-0.3 for GPU-heavy sequential workloads.
release_notes: Enhancements to Dedicated autoscaler: priority routing and token-bucket burst smoothing; new per-priority utilization metrics and dashboards. Backwards-compatible config; see docs/ops/dedicated-autoscaler-migration.md for rollout guidance.
